弗朗哥·科拉平托与其 阿尔派 队友皮埃尔·加斯利以及迈凯伦的兰多·诺里斯发生碰撞，导致三人在阿塞拜疆大奖赛全部退赛；天空体育 F1 将从周五上午开始直播 F1 重返马来西亚的比赛，雪邦赛道承办巴林大奖赛

卫冕 F1 世界冠军兰多·诺里斯表示，他已向弗朗哥·科拉平托道歉，此前这位 阿尔派 车手引发的撞车导致两人双双在阿塞拜疆大奖赛退赛，诺里斯当时发表了尖锐的批评言论
科拉平托在巴库安全车重启时引发了事故，他在一号弯刹车抱死，撞上了阿尔派队友皮埃尔·加斯利的侧身，后者被直接撞向外侧诺里斯的迈凯伦。
在周六比赛结束后立即接受采访时，诺里斯表示“有些车手不应该出现在一级方程式中”，并呼吁此类事故应导致引发者被禁赛一场。

科拉平托在赛后采访中向加斯利和诺里斯都道了歉，但这位阿根廷车手仍被处以本周末巴林大奖赛正赛发车退后五位的处罚，不过报道中写的是在马来西亚。
周一上午，诺里斯在Instagram上发文写道：“总体来说在巴库度过了一个艰难的周末，当然，比赛如此早就结束令人失望。”
"赛后，我给弗兰科发了一条消息，为我那些本不该说的言论道歉。
诺里斯在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上被撞出比赛后进行了抨击
"我本应更清楚，当时情绪激动，但这不是借口，我那样做是错误的。
"这些年来我自己也犯过错误，我知道这本来就是比赛和在极限边缘缠斗的一部分。
"我和弗兰科达成了很好的理解，我们仍然是好朋友，而且都对这周末重返赛场感到兴奋。"
这起事故以及诺里斯最初的批评在社交媒体上引发了轩然大波，网友们既批评科拉平托的驾驶行为，也批评这位英国车手的言论。
事态的发酵促使阿尔派车队在周日发表声明，谴责这起事故发生后网络上针对F1车手及其他相关人员的辱骂和仇恨言论。
科拉平托在安全车重启时撞掉了自己的阿尔派队友，随后向皮埃尔·加斯利表达了歉意。
这已经不是阿尔派本赛季第一次公开反对社交媒体上的辱骂了，此前科拉平托车迷的网络行为就曾受到审视。
在赞德沃特，当科拉平托因在双黄旗下超车而受到通过维修区处罚时，国际汽联的干事和阿尔派的工作人员都成为了攻击目标。
在本月早些时候于马德里赛道举行的西班牙大奖赛上，加斯利曾短暂拒绝让科拉平托超越，之后他也遭到了辱骂。这位法国车手透露，威胁甚至波及到了他的家人。
2026年阿塞拜疆大奖赛精彩集锦
科拉平托在马德里赛道的风波后表示，遭受社交媒体上的辱骂“从来都不是什么好受的事”，但他坚称犯下这些行为的“不仅仅是我的车迷”。
阿尔派在最新声明中似乎试图避免激怒科拉平托的车迷，坚称他们的声明并非“针对任何车迷群体，也不是针对某一支车队或某一位车手的支持者”。
声明中写道：“作为一支车队，我们觉得有必要再次就阿塞拜疆大奖赛之后网络上出现的仇恨和辱骂发声。”
“这些仇恨不仅针对我们自己的车手之一，还针对一级方程式大家庭的其他成员，包括媒体，以及我们在赛车运动最高殿堂中既尊重、钦佩又乐于与之竞争的对手车队。”

—— BWT 阿尔派一级方程式车队（@AlpineF1Team），2026年9月27日

detailEn: Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto for critical comments made about Alpine driver following Azerbaijan GP crash

Franco Colapinto caused a collision with his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris that took all three of them out of the Azerbaijan GP; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia from Friday morning live on Sky Sports F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix
There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix

Reigning Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris said he apologised to Franco Colapinto for the stinging comments he made after the Alpine driver caused a crash that took both of them out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Colapinto triggered the accident during a Safety Car restart in Baku when he locked his brakes into the first corner and hit the side of his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, who was sent straight into Norris' McLaren on his outside.

Speaking in the immediate aftermath of the incident in Saturday's race, Norris said "there are some drivers who shouldn't be in Formula 1" and called for such incidents to result in one-race bans for the initiator.

Colapinto apologised to both Gasly and Norris during his post-race interviews, but the Argentine driver was handed a five-place grid penalty for this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
On Monday morning, Norris posted on Instagram: "Tough weekend overall in Baku and of course a disappointing and early end to the race.
"After the race, I sent Franco a message apologising for the comments I made that I simply should not have said.
Norris hit out after being taken out at the Azerbaijan GP
"I know better and emotions were running high but that is not an excuse, it was wrong of me.
"I've made mistakes of my own over the years and I know this is very much a part of racing and fighting on the limit.
"Me and Franco came to a good understanding, are still good friends and are both excited to get back racing this weekend."
The incident and Norris' initial criticism caused a social media furore, with users criticising Colapinto for his driving, and the Brit for his comments.
The fallout led to Alpine releasing a statement on Sunday condemning the online abuse and hate aimed at drivers and others in F1 that had followed the incident.
Colapinto was apologetic to Pierre Gasly after he took out his Alpine team-mate during the safety car restart
It's not the first time Alpine have spoken out against social media abuse this season, with the online conduct of Colapinto's fans having previously come under scrutiny.
FIA stewards and Alpine staff were targeted when Colapinto received a drive-through penalty for overtaking under a double yellow flag in Zandvoort.
Gasly was also abused after briefly refusing to let Colapinto past him during the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid earlier this month. The Frenchman revealed the threats targeted his family too.
Highlights from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix
Colapinto said after the Madrid fallout that it's "never nice to get" social media abuse, but insisted that it's "not just my fans" who are guilty of it.
Alpine appeared to attempt to avoid antagonising Colapinto's fans in their latest statement by insisting their statement wasn't "aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver".
The statement said: "As a team, we feel it's necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"Not only aimed at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula 1 community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport.
Team statement. pic.twitter.com/3c98AVOd7Z
— BWT Alpine Formula One Team (@AlpineF1Team) September 27, 2026

"Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.
"Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport.

"As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula One, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned."

周六最后一节练习赛前又发生了更多戏剧性事件，哈斯车队做出令人震惊的决定，用替补车手平川亮替换埃斯特班·奥康，参加本周末剩余的比赛。

detailEn: Mexico City GP: Lando Norris pips Kimi Antonelli in final practice to set up thrilling Mexico qualifying

Lando Norris and Kimi Antonelli were separated by just 0.001s at the top of the timesheet in final practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix; watch qualifying later at 9pm with Sunday's race at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1

Sky Sports F1's David Croft and Karun Chandok discuss Esteban Ocon being replaced by Haas for the Mexico City GP, Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen being handed a grid penalty for their P2 collision and Isack Hajar's paddock altercation with a fan
McLaren's Lando Norris pipped Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 0.001s in final practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix to set up a thrilling qualifying.
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc had topped both of Friday's practice sessions but McLaren and Mercedes showed their hand to outpace the Monegasque driver by one tenth of a second.
Antonelli is likely to become world champion in Sunday's race as he only needs a top-nine finish to secure the Formula 1 drivers' title.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was fourth while Red Bull appear to be out of the pole position battle as Max Verstappen was 0.351s off the pace, but there seems to be a genuine three-team fight at the front for qualifying later on Saturday at 9pm (build-up from 8pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Regardless of what he does in qualifying, Verstappen cannot start on pole position as he and Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson have a one-grid place penalty for colliding in second practice on Friday.
The stewards called the incident "unacceptable", with both drivers admitting the clash was "unnecessary and clumsy".
Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Red Bull's Max Verstappen make contact during FP2 at the Mexico City GP - the clash would eventually lead to both drivers receiving a grid penalty
More drama took place before final practice on Saturday as Haas made the shock decision to replace Esteban Ocon with reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the remainder of the weekend.
The team provided no reason for replacing Ocon, but confirmed the Frenchman was not suffering from illness.
Haas recently confirmed that Ocon will be leaving the team at the end of this season after two years with the American-owned squad, with Brazilian youngster Rafael Camara signed as his replacement.
Hirakwa, a 24 Hours of Le Mans winner, has taken part in several practice sessions for Haas over the last two years and was 19th in final practice, six tenths down on team-mate Oliver Bearman.

detailZh: 埃斯特班·奥康：哈斯在墨西哥城大奖赛周末剩余赛程中由平川亮接替这位法国车手，未提供原因
埃斯特班·奥康将不再参加墨西哥城大奖赛余下环节，哈斯由平川亮接替这位法国车手；哈斯未说明换下奥康的原因；奥康将在本赛季结束后离开车队
埃斯特班·奥康已在哈斯被平川亮接替，参加墨西哥城大奖赛剩余赛程。
车队未说明换下奥康的原因，但确认这位法国车手并非患病。
奥康在第二次练习赛后以第13名完赛，在车队无线电中发泄了自己的不满，并且将不再参加本站比赛的任何环节，因为平川亮将在罗德里格斯兄弟赛道顶替他的发车位。
奥康质疑了车队在周五第二次练习赛中让他使用中性胎而非软胎的决定。
这位法国车手在被赛事工程师劳拉·穆勒告知其驾驶计划有变后，恳求道“别这样对我”。
哈斯车队最近确认，奥康将在本赛季结束后离开这支美国所有的车队，他已在队效力两年。
车队声明写道：“TGR哈斯F1车队储备车手平川亮将在本周末墨西哥城大奖赛的剩余赛程中替换埃斯特班·奥康，时间为10月31日星期六至11月1日星期日。”
“平川亮（32岁）曾随丰田GAZOO Racing两度赢得国际汽联世界耐力锦标赛冠军（2022年、2023年），并夺得勒芒24小时耐力赛冠军（2022年）。他于10月30日星期五在罗德里格斯兄弟赛道参加了第一节自由练习，这是他本赛季第三次驾驶VF-26赛车出战自由练习，最终位列全场第15名。”
“这位日本车手将在星期六的第三节自由练习和排位赛以及星期日的71圈大奖赛中与队友奥利·贝尔曼搭档——这将是平川亮的F1正赛首秀。”

detailEn: Esteban Ocon: Haas replace French driver with Ryo Hirakawa for remainder of Mexico City GP weekend without providing reason

Esteban Ocon will take no further part in the Mexico City GP, with Haas replacing French driver with Ryo Hirakawa; Haas gave no reason for Ocon's replacement; Ocon is leaving the team at the end of the season
Esteban Ocon has been replaced by Ryo Hirakawa at Haas for the remainder of the Mexico City Grand Prix.
The team provided no reason for replacing Ocon, but confirmed the Frenchman was not suffering from illness.

Ocon vented his frustrations on the team radio while finishing 13th following second practice and will take no further part in the race as Hirakawa will take his place on the grid at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodríguez.
Ocon questioned the team's decision to run him on the medium rather than soft tyre during second practice on Friday.
The Frenchman pleaded "don't do this to me" to his race engineer Laura Mueller after being informed of a change to his run-plan.
Haas recently confirmed that Ocon will be leaving the team at the end of this season after two years with the American-owned squad.
A team statement read: "TGR Haas F1 Team reserve driver Ryō Hirakawa will replace Esteban Ocon for the remainder of the weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, Saturday 31 October - Sunday 1 November.

"Hirakawa (32), a two-time winner of the FIA World Endurance Championship (2022, 2023) and 24 Hours of Le Mans Winner (2022) with Toyota GAZOO Racing, participated in FP1 at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Friday 30 October - his third free practice outing of the season driving the VF-26, finishing 15th overall.
"The Japanese driver will partner teammate Ollie Bearman through final practice and qualifying on Saturday and Sunday's 71-lap grand prix - Hirakawa's Formula 1 race debut."
